notes: Second full sweep at db91c23: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, uncommitted false, skill_hash a6a9c1d6..., each model_id matching its tier. Every run read SKILL.md first.

Changed rule, now in the case's list and graded per run against the current text: Chain fallible steps with `with`. The verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function). A run with no `with` is "not exercised", as in this sweep's order-report grades; the check batch (2026-10-21-check) graded such runs "clean", so its Haiku tier reads clean where this file reads not exercised.

`with`, violating runs out of five per sentence: one-step `with` 1 of 5 (sonnet-1, twice: line 65 in apply_code/2 and line 89 in total/2); `else` 0 of 5 (no run wrote an else); a `case` nested in a `with` body on a second fallible call 0 of 5. Opus-1 (lines 68-69) and sonnet-2 (lines 74-75) chain parse and already-applied checks as two steps, each a private function returning :ok or {:ok, value} and {:error, reason}. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 write no `with` and handle each single fallible call with case. For comparison: the previous sweep had one-step `with` blocks in 3 of 5 skill runs (recorded then under other_violations), the check batch in 1 of 4.

Sonnet-1's line 65 is the shape SKILL.md's new example names as the one to replace ("with {:ok, discount} <- parse_discount(code), do: {:ok, apply_discount(cart, discount)}"), written after the session read SKILL.md. The check batch suggested the example matching this prompt might explain the drop there; this run shows the example alone does not prevent the pattern.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming. The fetch sentence adds "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." and the variable sentence adds "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## Naming). Neither decides a verdict here: the Sonnet runs' subtotal/2 looks prices up and returns {:error, ...} but is named by its job, and no run names a variable data.

Naming, violating runs out of five per sentence: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0; boolean functions end in ? 0 (no run defines a boolean function); get/fetch/fetch! 0 (no get or fetch function); size/length 0 (not exercised); descriptive names for ignored values 0 (_held, _current, _reason, _other, _quantity, _discount, _code, _subtotal; no bare _ in new code); domain variable names 0. Held to the earlier standard, which passed role names such as sum, other, normalized and value: haiku-2's input (the raw typed string, lines 61-64 and 88-89), sonnet-2's parsed (line 74) and the Sonnet runs' sum accumulator are not counted.

Unchanged rules graded to the previous sweep's standard: Update structs, Convert external strings to atoms, Return {:ok, value} or {:error, reason}, Store and compute money, Before you finish. The 'How to use this skill' line now says to read reference files "before you write code"; it is not a graded rule, but it bears on Expected reads below.

Before you finish: 1 of 5 violated. Sonnet-1 ran mix format and mix test (which compiled the project without warnings) but never ran mix credo --strict or a separate mix compile; its refused python3 heredoc carried mix format, mix compile and mix test but no Credo step, so the refusal does not explain the missing Credo run. The other four ran format, compile with --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict and test after their edits.

Refused commands (the permission gate pre-approved only commands starting with mix, elixir or elixirc): haiku-1 a find -exec listing and a sed -i edit chain that also carried mix format, mix test and mix credo --strict, after which it made the edits with Edit and re-ran format, compile, test and credo; haiku-2 two file-listing loops ($(find ...) and while read); sonnet-1 an xargs/cat listing and the python3 heredoc above; sonnet-2 an xargs/cat listing and a python3 heredoc that carried the full mix chain, re-run after Write.
